source.title: Time-Aware Feature Selection: Adaptive Temporal Masking for Stable Sparse Autoencoder Training

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It identifies itself as an XAI4Science workshop paper at ICLR 2025.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures model cross-entropy after SAE reconstruction, a component of V3, but does not compare with random errors of the same size.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE reconstruction and downstream metrics, but only the cross-entropy loss score directly bears on a claim version. It does not measure linear predictability of SAE error, error norms across SAE sizes or contexts, feature/error decomposition, or comparisons with random errors.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE-training paper about feature absorption. It neither tests nor uses the dark-matter finding, and does not cite the original. Its only related number is the cross-entropy loss score after substituting reconstructions, normalized between the original and zero-ablation losses. That score has no same-size random-error comparison, so it cannot show V3's pathological-error effect. It also does not measure linear predictability of error (V1), error scaling across SAE sizes (V2), a decomposition of the error (V4), circuit or steering loss (V5), or how dark matter changes with training (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ATM sharply reduces feature absorption (0.0068 vs 0.0114 for JumpReLU and 0.1402 for TopK) while keeping strong reconstruction. They also claim superior sparse probing accuracy, but their own Table 1 shows TopK higher (0.7698 vs 0.7161). They draw no conclusions about the structure or function of SAE error.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates a temporal masking SAE-training method and reports reconstruction loss scores; it does not apply the original dark-matter analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported cross-entropy loss score varies by SAE method.

fits_no_version.finding: Reconstruction fidelity differs strongly by SAE training method on Gemma-2-2B layer 12. Explained variance is 0.60 for TopK (L0=40), 0.73 for JumpReLU, 0.91 for ATM and 0.98 for the standard SAE. The comparison is confounded by very different L0 values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Total SAE reconstruction error depends on the training method and sparsity level (overall error size, not a dark-matter decomposition).

record.problems: The study does not include a random-error comparison, so its reconstruction loss scores cannot establish whether SAE errors harm loss more than same-size random errors. Experiments are limited to Gemma-2-2B, layer 12, and 5M training tokens; the authors report constrained compute and no systematic hyperparameter investigation.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported metrics, including MSE, cosine similarity, explained variance, sparsity, absorption, and sparse probing, do not directly measure any claim version. No results were omitted for row-count limits.

untested.parts: All: no regression of SAE error on input activations.
All: no per-token error norms, no comparison across SAE sizes (single width n=16384).
All: no comparison of reconstruction-induced loss against same-size random errors.
All: no decomposition of error into linear and nonlinear parts.
All: no circuit or steering analysis with or without the error term.
All: architectures are compared only on overall reconstruction metrics at very different L0s. There is no dark-matter decomposition and no end-to-end training.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is set to 'discusses' only for lack of a better enum value: the paper does not cite the dark-matter original and only reports generic reconstruction metrics. Evidence is weak overall: a workshop paper, one model and layer, 5M training tokens, no uncertainty estimates, and baselines with unmatched L0s (40 to 8724).

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Whether per-token error norms are predictable across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
The study evaluates loss after SAE reconstruction, but does not compare that loss with random errors of the same size.
Whether the linear part contains unlearned features and whether the nonlinear part resists further dictionary learning.
Whether analyses based on SAE features lose behavior unless the error term is retained.
Whether dark matter reflects SAE training choices or shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Substitute SAE reconstruction for the original activation and report the normalized cross-entropy loss score.
rows.measure: Cross-Entropy Loss Score; higher values closer to 1 indicate better information retention.
rows.baseline: The score is defined using Horig and H0; their numeric values are not stated.
rows.note: The score measures loss after reconstruction relative to the stated original and zero-ablation references, but there is no random-error comparison of the same size.
rows.check: A normalized CE loss score (0.9967) without a random-error control cannot show whether SAE errors harm loss more than random errors. It is the study's own method compared with baselines, not a test of V3.
